title: Cowpea Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Cowpea Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Cowpea nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium in paayap, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Cowpea nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your paayap (cowpea) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, magnesium, manganese, iron and boron. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.credit: Maja Dumat, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But manganese, iron and boron stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which cowpea nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.
Cowpea nutrient deficiency signs, old leaves and young leaves
Shows first on the old leaves

blocks.caption: Deficiencies that start on the old leaves of paayap
rows: old, lower leaves, the whole plant

Small, dark green plants that grow slowly and set few pods.

blocks.text: Shows first on the young leaves

blocks.caption: Deficiencies that start on the young leaves of paayap

Young leaves pale between green veins, later with brown spots, often on limed sandy soil.
young leaves and the tip, between the veins
Young leaves turn yellow, veins and all, then nearly white, on limey soil.
New leaves come out small and crinkled.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a cowpea nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest cowpea nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in cowpea

Lower leaves turn pale and yellow first and the whole plant stays light green, thin and slow. Cowpea feeds itself through root nodules, so this nearly always means the nodules are few or not working. You see it most at this stage: three to six weeks after planting.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in paayap

In a legume this usually means poor nodulation: no inoculant in a field new to the crop, inoculant killed by sun or heat, very acid soil, waterlogging, hot dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer near the seed, which stops nodules from forming.
How to tell it apart

Sulfur deficiency starts on the young leaves. Iron and manganese deficiency yellow between the veins of young leaves. To be sure, dig, do not pull, a few plants 3 to 6 weeks after planting, wash the roots and cut some nodules open. Pink to red inside means they are working, white means not active yet, and brown, grey or mushy means dead.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency
Feed the standing crop, since nodules cannot be added now: sidedress a little Urea 46 0 0 beside the rows, following the soil test. Texas AandM advises nitrogen fertilizer when nodulation is poor.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, use a cowpea Rhizobium inoculant on the seed at planting, keep it shaded, and give only a small nitrogen starter.
Phosphorus deficiency in cowpea
Plants are small and stunted with dark, sometimes bluish green leaves and often no clear leaf marks. Roots and nodules are few and pods are few. You see it most at this stage: seedling to flowering.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in paayap
Acid upland soils and soils low in phosphorus.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen deficiency makes plants pale, not dark. To be sure, soil test for phosphorus, or compare with a strip given phosphorus.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency
Apply 16 20 0 or Complete 14 14 14 in the furrow at planting, following the soil test. For a standing crop give a 2 percent DAP 18 46 0 spray (20 g per liter) every 15 days for pulses.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, apply phosphorus at every planting and add compost.
Potassium deficiency in cowpea

The tips and edges of older leaflets turn yellow, and the yellow moves slowly toward the center and base. The leaf edges then die and brown, and the leaves fall. You see it most at this stage: flowering and pod filling.
Why potassium deficiency happens in paayap
Sandy soils and soils cropped for years without potash.
How to tell it apart
Magnesium deficiency yellows between the veins, not from the edges. To be sure, soil test for potassium.
What to apply for potassium deficiency
Give a 1 percent potassium chloride spray (10 g Muriate of potash per liter). Add Muriate of potash 0 0 60 to the soil following the soil test.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, include potash at planting on sandy soils.
Magnesium deficiency in cowpea

The areas between the veins of older leaves turn yellow, later deep yellow, with rusty specks and dead blotches between the veins and at the edges. Late in the season the plants look like they are maturing early. You see it most at this stage: mid growth to pod filling.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in paayap
Acid, sandy soils in rainy areas and heavy potash.
How to tell it apart
Potassium deficiency starts at the leaf edges and tips. To be sure, soil test for magnesium and pH.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency
Give a 1 percent magnesium sulfate spray (10 g Epsom salt per liter) every 15 days. Use Dolomite on acid soils as the soil test advises.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid soils with dolomite.
Manganese deficiency in cowpea

Leaves turn pale green to pale yellow between the veins, which stay green, starting on the new leaves. Brown spots and dead patches follow on the lower leaves as it gets worse. You see it most at this stage: early to mid growth.
Why manganese deficiency happens in paayap
High pH, over limed sandy soils and soils high in organic matter.
How to tell it apart
Iron deficiency turns the veins yellow too. To be sure, leaf test for manganese and a soil pH test.
What to apply for manganese deficiency
Give 5 kg manganese sulfate per hectare to the soil, or two manganese sulfate sprays 10 days apart.

Sold here with manganese: **Manganese Sulfate** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (31 percent manganese), **Tierramino Mn** by Unilox Far East Resources Inc. (12 percent manganese and 7 percent N), **Multimate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (1.8 percent Mn, 2.8 percent Zn, 4 percent N, 4.5 percent S (w/v)) and **Biozome** by Manchem Industries, Inc. (12 percent S, 12 percent Zn, 3 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 1 percent Fe, 1 percent Cu, 0.5 percent B, 0.05 percent Mo). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [manganese deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/manganese-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, do not over lime.
Iron deficiency in cowpea

Young leaves yellow between the veins first, then the veins yellow too, and in severe cases the leaves turn almost white. Older leaves stay green while growth slows. You see it most at this stage: seedling and early growth.
Why iron deficiency happens in paayap
High pH soils with free lime.
How to tell it apart
Manganese deficiency keeps the veins green. To be sure, soil pH test and a leaf test.
What to apply for iron deficiency
Give a 0.5 percent ferrous sulfate spray (5 g per liter).

Sold here with iron: **Ferrous Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Cleveland Industries Inc. (20 percent iron), **Ferrous Sulfate Monohydrate** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (30 percent iron), **Grow More Liquid Chelate Iron with Sulfur** by Sagrex Corporation (5 percent iron and 3 percent sulfur) and **Biozome** by Manchem Industries, Inc. (12 percent S, 12 percent Zn, 3 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 1 percent Fe, 1 percent Cu, 0.5 percent B, 0.05 percent Mo). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [iron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/iron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, avoid limey patches or add compost.
Boron deficiency in cowpea

Leaves crinkle and stay small, mostly at the top of the plant. The newest growth is hit worst while older leaves look normal, since boron does not move within the plant. You see it most at this stage: flowering and pod set.
Why boron deficiency happens in paayap
Sandy soils low in organic matter, high pH soils and drought.
How to tell it apart
Virus diseases also crinkle leaves, with mosaic patterns and insects present. Boron shortage has no mosaic. To be sure, leaf or soil test for boron.
What to apply for boron deficiency
Give a 0.2 percent borax spray (2 g per liter). Do not band boron in the seed row (UW).

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, keep organic matter up.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any cowpea nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your paayap needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Cowpea nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my paayap leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: pale yellow green plants with weak growth and few working nodules on the roots. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at manganese deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in cowpea?
items.a: Feed the standing crop, since nodules cannot be added now: sidedress a little Urea 46 0 0 beside the rows, following the soil test. Texas AandM advises nitrogen fertilizer when nodulation is poor.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in cowpea?
items.a: Apply 16 20 0 or Complete 14 14 14 in the furrow at planting, following the soil test. For a standing crop give a 2 percent DAP 18 46 0 spray (20 g per liter) every 15 days for pulses.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in cowpea?
items.a: Give a 1 percent potassium chloride spray (10 g Muriate of potash per liter). Add Muriate of potash 0 0 60 to the soil following the soil test.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my paayap lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the cowpea nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
